A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HopS study. Their complete main text and appendices, including rendered equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite pagination and table-order changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results, module ablations, sensitivity studies and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds OCTA-3mm classification results and an optimal-transport entropy-coefficient sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The LDF neighbor filter, GOP transport formulation, Sinkhorn updates, combined loss and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The added evaluations introduce no new method component or training procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a supplementary medical-image classification evaluation on OCTA-3mm: 200 images spanning NORMAL, DR, AMD and CNV. This extends domain coverage while retaining the original eight-benchmark classification suite and ImageNet memory experiment.

E2.justification: Existing loss baselines, CLIP/CoOp, CroSel, PaPi and SoLar remain in their corresponding comparisons. The new OCTA and entropy-sensitivity tables report HopS alone; newly cited prompt-learning methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate OCTA with randomly generated candidate sets of 1–4 labels and sweep the entropy coefficient over nine values from 0.02 to 10 on Caltech and Flowers under both prompt types and confusion types. Existing experimental settings and the default coefficient of 0.05 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.8 and Tables 20–21 test sensitivity to GOP's entropy coefficient. Existing component, batch-size, neighborhood, threshold, missing-label and long-tail analyses remain. The 4-shot/8-shot study is retained from v1, merely moving from C.8 to C.9.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three runs with three different random seeds. v2 specifies no increased run count or new uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and figure graphics are retained. New Table 9 reports OCTA accuracies of 81.80%, 84.80%, 42.40% and 9.10% for 1–4 candidate labels; Tables 20–21 add entropy-sweep accuracies. These are additional experimental results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, transport constraints, Sinkhorn equations and learning objective are unchanged. Removing the duplicate confusion-rate explanation from Appendix A.1 does not remove its definition, which remains in Section 5.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: combining local and global label selection for robust prompt learning, supported by strong performance on eight benchmarks. The supplementary experiments do not redefine the headline claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.8 interprets the entropy sweep as showing effectiveness across coefficients and a strong, stable range around 0.05. Section 5.3 also adds that cosine similarity is robust to sparsity. Existing mechanism explanations and qualifications are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract. It also documents OCTA's size, classes and candidate-label construction. Appendix A.2's implementation settings, hardware and software details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds citations to PLOT, JoAPR, NLPrompt and Wu et al.'s study of prompt tuning under noisy labels. These modestly broaden contextual coverage; the positioning relative to conventional PLL and SoLar remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording edits, a shortened GOP explanation, author-affiliation and corresponding-author information, acknowledgements and new appendix passages. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9, 20 and 21, expands Table 1's caption, and reorders or relocates existing appendix tables and plots. All existing figure graphics are retained; the changes are limited display and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new entropy sweep makes the previously fixed regularization choice empirically assessable, and the code-access pointer improves reproducibility information. OCTA adds useful evidence from another domain, but its specific train/test split and baseline comparisons are unreported, and the decline to 9.10% with four candidates is unexplained. These additions modestly strengthen the paper without materially changing its main scientific case.
